name: Touch controls with edge-latched input
oneLiner: A pixel-style D-pad or virtual stick with A/B buttons and a START pill appears on phones, below the game canvas, in its side gutters or over its bottom corners (never on the HUD); every finger is tracked (hold a direction while pressing A, slide from B to A), presses sink and light up, and every input (keyboard, touch, gamepad) is edge-latched so a tap shorter than one game step still counts exactly once. Touches become the game's own key events, so its logic stays as it is.
fits: puzzle and arcade games played with a few keys
notFor: games built around pointer aiming or drag (use direct touch on the canvas instead)
rhythm games that need exact touch timing on the playfield
games that already ship their own touch layout and want to keep it

needs: a fixed 60 Hz update step: one step() call as its first line (also in ?t= fast-forward, title and pause)
the game canvas element and the key codes its keydown handler binds (directions, confirm, cancel, pause)
optional: rectangles to avoid (HUD, dialogue and menu boxes, in canvas px) for controls drawn over the canvas
provides: input: keydown / keyup events with the game's own codes for each touch and gamepad press (events mode)
input: edge-latched pressed() / held() / released() / repeat() / axis() per role, the same for keyboard, touch and gamepad (poll mode)
onFirstInput callback (unlock audio), the controls' rects on screen (layout())

assets: module/touch-controls.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_TouchControls): pointer and touch tracking, key-event synthesis, edge latch, gamepad polling, layout (below / sides / over, safe areas, whole-pixel scale), the pixel-art D-pad, stick, buttons and START pill; draws through GameDNA_Skin when skin-api.js is loaded, otherwise with its built-in copy of the pixel16 look
